title: Post-deploy sanity orchestrator for private deployments
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working sketch for a lightweight, repeatable "post-deploy sanity orchestrator" that runs after Argo/Helm-based private deployments (VPC or on-prem). Goal is to give SREs and operators fast automated validation signals (and automated rollbacks when safe) while keeping the flow portable across air-gapped and VPC installs.

High level flow (happy path):
1) ArgoCD/Operator applies Helm chart -> rollout begins
2) Image signature verification step (cosign) as part of image promotion gating
3) Post-sync hook triggers orchestrator job (k8s Job or remote exec into a control plane VM)
4) Orchestrator runs parallel smoke tests (API sanity, KV cache warm, kv-prefetch, 1–2 sample inferences, metrics ingestion check)
5) Each test emits a JSON result + timing + probe metrics to ephemeral results store (S3/VPC-ordered object store, or local MinIO for airgapped)
6) Aggregator evaluates pass/fail against thresholds and either: mark deployment healthy; mark degraded and schedule extended checks; or flag and initiate rollback/canary remedial actions.

Key design constraints (private deployments):
- Cannot rely on external hosted services: results must be stored in customer-provided object store or in-cluster CRs.
- Minimal outbound network permitted in many installs. Mirror/copy any required test artifacts into the airgap promotion bundle.
- Must support operator-initiated mid-rollout aborts (human-in-loop).
- Low blast radius: tests run at low qps, conservative timeouts, and only against canary replicas when present.

Components & responsibilities:
- Terraform outputs mapping: expose endpoints (control-plane host), credentials location (k8s secret name), and artifact provenance (image digests). Add outputs: post_deploy_bucket, post_deploy_sa_secret, smoke_test_target_ips.
- ArgoCD Application: include preSync hook for cosign verification (or an admission/webhook that rejects unsigned images), and postSync hook to call the orchestrator.
- Helm test wrapper: a tiny binary/script (redwood-post-deploy-check) installed into the chart's test harness that executes smoke tests and returns structured JSON.
- Results aggregator: lightweight controller (or CronJob) that collects test outputs and writes a deployment status CRD or uploads to the configured store.
- Rollback actuator: a controlled step that either: patches Argo Application to previous revision, or signals the operator to run rollback via the operator CLI.

Concrete Argo hooks (examples, sketch):
- preSync: run-image-signature-check.sh 
  - Purpose: ensure images in manifests match signed digests in attestation store. Works in airgapped mode by checking bundled attestations.
  - Failure: block sync and attach error message in Argo UI.

- postSync (sync-wave +1): invoke post-deploy-orchestrator job:
  kubectl create job --from=cronjob/post-deploy-orchestrator post-deploy-<rev>-<ts> 
  (or use Argo Rollouts webhook to call the control plane API)

Helm test wrapper (pseudo):
- /tests/helm/redwood-post-deploy-check.sh\  - steps:
    1) resolve service IP via terraform output or k8s svc
    2) run health endpoint: /internal/health?checks=all -> expect 200 + JSON with fields (build, kv-warm, cache-hit-rate >= 90%)
    3) run small inference: prompt="sanity: repeat 3 words" with model pinned to canary variant, expect output length /incidence of generic failure < 3%
    4) check telemetry endpoint ingestion: push test metric via local statsd/OTLP and confirm ingestion via query to metrics-store API (within 30s)
    5) verify TLS cert chain and CN match expected (for VPC installs we often pin CN patterns)
    6) on success, write /tmp/post-deploy-result.json (structured) with fields: test_name, status, latency_ms, logs_url (if any)

Test matrix & thresholds (draft):
- api-health: success if 200 and all subchecks pass -> gate=hard
- inference-sanity: 3 requests, median latency < 250ms (canary smaller machine), failure rate < 10% -> gate=soft (allows followup)
- cold-start-mem-check: sample kernel/pid health within 60s -> gate=soft
- kv-cache-warm: cache-hit rate > 85% within 120s -> gate=hard for large traffic customers; soft otherwise
- telemetry-latency: ingest within 30s -> gate=soft

Failure modes and automated responses:
- single hard gate fail: block promotion and set Argo Application to OutOfSync with message. Notify operator channel + open linear ticket with collected artifacts.
- multiple soft gates failing: continue rollout but reduce traffic routing (if using service mesh/canary), schedule extended tests and require manual ack to proceed.
- flaky failures (intermittent < 2x): tag as flaky, suggest golden prompt set re-run, escalate to applied-ml if SLO regression suspected.

Rollback orchestration (safe defaults):
- Immediate rollback only if a hard gate fails AND failure is reproducible in second run. Steps:
  1) call Argo API to rollback to previous synced revision (POST /api/v1/applications/<app>/rollback)
  2) run cancellation of post-deploy jobs and mark release as rolled-back in the results store
  3) if rollback API not available, use operator CLI: redwoodctl rollout undo --app <app> --rev <prev>
  4) post-rollback smoke-run to validate restoration of baseline (short-check-suite)
- Human-in-loop rollback: when tests are ambiguous or customer policy requires approval, leave rollout paused and alert on-call.

Airgap / VPC nuance checklist:
- Ensure cosign attestations are included in release bundle (attestation.json) and verifiers use local root keys.
- Provide a local results target (MinIO) with credentials passed via Terraform outputs. Document encryption-at-rest requirement.
- No external DNS calls: all tests must be resolvable against internal endpoints or IPs from terraform outputs.
- Avoid scripts that curl public package repos; vendor any test dependencies into the release artifact.

Terraform patterns to expose test hooks (notes):
- outputs.tf additions (example names):
  - post_deploy_bucket = aws_s3_bucket.postdeploy.id
  - smoke_test_service_ips = module.k8s_service.smoke_test_ips
  - postdeploy_k8s_secret = kubernetes_secret.postdeploy_creds.metadata[0].name
- Keep secrets out of plain-text state: store test credentials in KMS-wrapped secrets and output only secret names/ids.
- Provide a boolean toggle in tfvars: enable_postdeploy_orchestrator (default true). For airgap installs, require explicit enable.

Packaging & release notes for operators:
- Release artifact must include: helm chart tar.gz, images (digest list), cosign signature bundle, post-deploy test artifacts (binary or container image), terraform variables snippet, and a short runbook.md.
- Versioning: semantic release for chart + bundle. Keep test harness pinned to chart minor version to prevent mismatches.

Observability and artifacts to collect (must be in results):
- raw stdout/stderr from each test step (logs)
- JSON result with latency percentiles and pass/fail per probe
- k8s events around deployment window (last 5 minutes)
- image digests verified
- optional traces for sample inference request (if tracing enabled)

Operator UX & Slack integration (quick sketch):
- Orchestrator posts a message to ops channel: [ORCH] deploy app=foo rev=42 status=DEGRADED tests_failed=inference-sanity
- Attach small summary + link to artifacts store + action buttons (Rollback | Re-run tests | Open ticket). For airgapped installs the message is an operator-visible artifact link; customers may require separate ticketing.

Runbook snippets (to include in bundle):
- How to re-run tests locally: 
  export KUBECONFIG=/path/to/kubeconfig\  redwood-post-deploy-check --target http://svc.x.svc.cluster.local --output ./results.json
- How to force rollback: 
  argocd app rollback <app> <rev>  OR redwoodctl rollout undo --app <app> --rev <rev>
- Where artifacts live: <post_deploy_bucket>/<app>/<rev>/results.json

Open questions / TODOs:
- Where should the canonical results CRD live? In-cluster or in customer-provided object store? (tradeoff: availability vs airgap compatibility)
- Should we add a signed attestation of the test results themselves (to avoid tampering in regulated setups)?
- How do we gracefully degrade orchestration for very resource constrained clusters (run tests off-cluster against forwarded ports)?
- Add test that validates model quality regression (LM eval prompt set) — this might be heavy and should be optional per-customer.
- Can we piggyback on existing Argo Rollouts webhooks to reduce surface area?

Next steps / action items:
- [Elliot] prototype a k8s Job version of the orchestrator that writes results to MinIO (deadline: 2024-11-01)
- [Marcus] add terraform outputs for results bucket + secret names (PR draft: infra/td/feature/postdeploy-outputs)
- [Asha] build initial helm-test wrapper and sample Argo hook (PR: charts/post-deploy-tests)
- [Priya] draft runbook template for bundle inclusion and compliance checklist

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally lightweight and focused on practical ops. The goal is not to create a full CI pipeline replacement but to provide safe, auditable, and portable post-deploy checks that reduce noisy rollbacks and speed up detection of regression. Please annotate where we should simplify for customers with strict airgap policies.

Attachments / quick links (internal):
- prototype scripts: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-scripts/tree/postdeploy-orchestrator
- Linear ticket: PD-482
- example results JSON (short):
  {
    "app": "foo",
    "rev": "42",
    "tests": [
      {"name": "api-health", "status": "PASS", "latency_ms": 12},
      {"name": "inference-sanity", "status": "FAIL", "failure_rate": 0.33}
    ],
    "aggregated_status": "DEGRADED"
  }
